resources.string: Detects when you pause on a screen so Heimdall can offer a short hint. Heimdall reads no text from other apps and never leaves the device.
An on-device co-pilot that offers a short hint when a screen stops making sense. No network, no accounts, no telemetry.
Heimdall has no INTERNET permission. Frames are processed by a local model and never written to disk.
Choose both GGUF files. Heimdall reads them where they are — nothing is copied, moved or uploaded.

Heimdall needs the two MiniCPM-V 2.6 files:

1. minicpm-v-2_6-Q4_K_M.gguf (about 5.5 GB)
2. mmproj-f16.gguf (about 1 GB)

Download them from openbmb/MiniCPM-V-2_6 on Hugging Face to the phone (for example Downloads), then tap “Choose file” here and pick each one.

The files stay exactly where they are: the picker grants read access only, so Heimdall never copies or deletes them. The README mentioned in earlier builds lives at the root of the project repository, github.com/Hakim3691/heimdall (section “Models are never committed”).

Cloud-only documents cannot be used because they must be memory-mapped from local storage.
That file cannot be used: %1$s. Pick a local copy of the GGUF file.
